hypotheses: nu > 0 is an arbitrary positive viscosity
preamble_entries.conclusion: There exist a force f in C_c^inf(R^3 x (0,inf); R^3), a compact set K in R^3, and smooth velocity and pressure fields u, p on R^3 x [0,1) solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations (1.1) d_t u + (u.grad)u - nu Lap u + grad p = f, div u = 0, u(.,0) = 0, such that supp u(.,t) union supp p(.,t) is contained in K for every 0 <= t < 1, sup_{0<=t<1} ||u(t)||_{L^2(R^3)} < inf, and limsup_{t->1} ||u(t)||_{L^inf(R^3)} = inf. Consequently there is no smooth solution (u,P) on R^3 x [0,inf) with the same force and initial datum whose kinetic energy sup_{t>=0} (1/2) int |u|^2 dx is uniformly bounded.
constants: nu > 0 arbitrary
singular time t = 1
force supported in K x [0,2] (per Section 3.5)
scaling to viscosity nu: u_nu(x,t) = sqrt(nu) u(x/sqrt(nu), t), p_nu = nu p(x/sqrt(nu), t), f_nu = sqrt(nu) f(x/sqrt(nu), t) (p. 7)
preamble_entries.role: Main theorem: finite-time blowup of the L^inf norm with bounded energy and a smooth compactly supported force, establishing alternative (C) of the Millennium problem; the outline (Section 3.5) reduces it to Theorem 3.1 plus localization and uniqueness.

hypotheses: viscosity one (nu = 1), residual R(u,p) = d_t u + (u.grad)u - Lap u + grad p as in (3.1)
fields are considered on Omega_* = {(x,t): tau > 0, q < q_*} with tau = 1 - t and q = q(z,tau) the concentration scale of (3.2)
preamble_entries.conclusion: There are constants 0 < h < 1/100, q_* > 0, 0 < X_a < X_ext < inf and smooth fields (u,p) on Omega_* such that: (i) u = curl A + B e_theta (3.3) with A a vector potential and B an axisymmetric scalar, both smooth in Cartesian coordinates at the axis, and u exactly divergence-free; (ii) every Cartesian space-time derivative of A, B e_theta, p is uniformly bounded on compact spatial subsets with c <= q <= c' < q_* up to the one-sided boundary tau = 0, with limits compatible under differentiation; (iii) for every alpha, b, N and finite X_1, |d_x^alpha d_t^b R(u,p)| <= C_{alpha,b,N,X_1} q^N for 0 <= X <= X_1 as q -> 0 (3.4); for X >= X_ext the residual vanishes identically and A = 0, B = K(r,tau), p = -int_r^inf K(rho,tau)^2/rho d rho with K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2) (3.5), H_ext smooth on [0,inf) with each fixed derivative bounded, and K solving the radial swirl heat equation -d_tau K = d_r^2 K + r^{-1} d_r K - r^{-2} K; (iv) for some fixed X_in in (0, X_a) and e_0 > 0, u_theta(sqrt(2 X_in tau), 0, 0, 1 - tau) = tau^{-A}(e_0 + O(tau^{2h})) as tau -> 0 (3.6).
constants: 0 < X_a < X_ext < inf
exterior swirl K(r,tau) = r^{-1-2h} H_ext(tau/r^2)
X_in in (0, X_a)
error O(tau^{2h}) in (3.6)
flatness q^N for every N
preamble_entries.role: Local theorem: the summed local fields have a potential representation, are regular up to time one away from the origin, have a flat residual, coincide with the heat exterior for large X, and blow up along the growth path; Theorem 1.1 follows by localization (Section 3.5).

hypotheses: a leading field (velocity and pressure) for t < 1, or a scalar auxiliary profile in (X, eta)
preamble_entries.conclusion: A leading field is regular at the axis if its velocity and pressure extend smoothly across r = 0 in Cartesian coordinates for t < 1. For scalar auxiliary profiles, regular at the axis means a smooth extension in (X, eta) to X = 0.
preamble_entries.role: Fixes the meaning of axis regularity used for the profiles E/sqrt(2X), U, V_0/X, Pi and for the leading field.

hypotheses: alpha >= 0 and beta > 0
preamble_entries.conclusion: alpha << beta means alpha/beta is required to be sufficiently small, with the allowed size depending on all data already fixed. In a chain of constants, choices proceed from right to left; small reciprocals specify large parameters. For expressions depending on profile variables, the smallness is uniform on the stated domain and is ensured by those parameter choices.
preamble_entries.role: Fixes the convention for parameter smallness and the order in which constants are chosen throughout the construction.

hypotheses: labels gamma = (l, a, sigma) in Gamma as in (6.8), with band scale Q = 2^{-l}, eps = Q^h, S_* = l^2, pulse interval 0 <= v <= L_s with L_s = 2 r_0/c_i ~ S_*

phase Phi = p theta + p_z Z/eps + x_0 R - v(pF + p_z G) as in (7.3) with wave numbers from (7.2): k = ceil(eps^{-1/2}), B_s^2 = lambda_0/(eps k^2 (1+u_*^2)^{3/2}), s(v) = sigma(u_*/2 + u_* v/L_s), (p~/R_0, p_z) = B_s(K - sigma u_* g_0/(L_s |g_0|^2)), kp a nearest nonzero integer to k p~, x_0 = sigma B_s u_*/2

u_* > 0 chosen so that u_*/sqrt(1+u_*^2) exceeds sup |c_0 (T_{0,*}.K)/(T_{0,*}.N)|, using the strict cone margin (7.1)
background (u_B, p_B) of Proposition 5.5 with b = O(eps) and tangential velocity within O(eps^2) of order zero by (5.42)
entries.conclusion: There is a sufficiently small q_* > 0, common to all labels and fixed derivative orders, such that on every rectangle with 0 < q < q_*: every e^{ikm Phi}, m nonzero integer, is single-valued in theta with nonzero angular frequency; on 0 <= v <= L_s, |n_Phi - B_s(s(v), K)| + |n_Phi'| <= C/S_* and the eikonal defect E_ik = (t_* + b D_r + F d_theta + G D_z) Phi = O(eps S_*^C) (7.9), in every fixed coefficient derivative with polynomial degree; coefficients extend smoothly to the fixed enlargement; all fixed mixed derivatives of n_Phi and the frames have polynomial bounds in S_*. The real 3x2 matrix B of (7.8) has columns spanning n_Phi^perp, a uniformly bounded left inverse B^l, and B^l(A_Phi B - B') = diag(lambda, -lambda) + E with lambda(v) = lambda_0/sqrt(1+s(v)^2) and |E| <= C/S_* (7.10). With d_ref = eps k^2 B_s^2 (1+s^2), |d - d_ref| <= C/S_* (7.11).

entries.role: Establishes that the chosen phase approximately follows background transport and that, in the frame B, the projected pulse operator is a diagonal growth/decay pair plus O(1/S_*) errors, which is the input for solving the amplitude equation (7.5).

hypotheses: alpha in R fixed; a finite set of harmonics 0 < |m| <= M
a label at level i on a common torus H = Y_{i_0}, with i - i_0 bounded as in Lemma 6.2

f_m has a fixed closed slow support inside the label's slow support, compact transverse support inside supp chi_g, and support in the closed active shell X_a <= X <= X_b, with smooth zero extension across all these boundaries
on X_a < X < X_b and 0 <= v <= L_s, for every fixed multi-index I in (R, Z, T, H): |D^I f_m| <= C_I eps^alpha S_*^{b_I} sqrt(zeta) delta^{-a_I} P(v)

K t_m - n_Phi' . t_m + n_Phi . f_m)/|n_Phi|^2 (7.13), with the source evaluated along the path H_w of (6.21). The coefficients descend to the same common torus and preserve the slow, transverse and shell supports with smooth zero extension; the solution is defined on the entire closed pulse interval 0 <= v <= L_s. On X_a < X < X_b, for every fixed I: |D^I t_m| <= C'_I eps^alpha S_*^{b'_I} sqrt(zeta) delta^{-a'_I} P(v) (7.14) and |D^I pi_m| <= C'_I eps^{alpha+1/2} S_*^{b'_I} sqrt(zeta) delta^{-a'_I} P(v) (7.15). Constants and degrees may depend on M, I and the source bounds; q_* does not depend on M, alpha, or the correction stage. One-sided slow derivatives at tau = 0 on compact sets with q > 0 are inherited from the source.

a_net(y) = lambda_0/sqrt(1+y^2) - lambda_0(1+y^2)/(1+u_*^2)^{3/2}, vanishing at y = u_*, with derivative in v between -C/L_s and -c/L_s
harmonic damping factor exp(-(m^2-1) int_w^v d) <= 1 (7.18)
propagator bound ||V_m(v,w)|| <= C P(v)/P(w) for 0 <= w <= v <= L_s (7.19)
pressure gains eps^{1/2} from (km)^{-1} = O(eps^{1/2})
degree increase at step I at most 1 + max{b_I, max_{0<J<=I}(c_J + b'_{I-J})}
L_s = O(S_*) integration length
D_H v = T_g^{i-i_0} lambda_t/c_i = O(S_*)

entries.role: The zero-data linear inverse for the projected amplitude equation with a prescribed harmonic source; used to remove later nonzero harmonics in the correction cycle (Proposition 9.1), with the response inheriting the pulse envelope.

hypotheses: the solution operators f_m -> (t_m, pi_m) of Proposition 7.2 with t_m(0) = 0
any finite correction stage, finite harmonic set, and derivative order
entries.conclusion: These solution operators are defined at every finite correction stage on the same domain 0 < q < q_*. Increasing the finite harmonic set or the derivative order changes constants and polynomial degrees but does not require shrinking the domain.
constants: q_* from Lemma 7.1 (single finite choice), stage-independent
entries.role: Guarantees that the space-time domain of the wave inverses does not shrink with the correction stage, so the induction of Section 9 runs on a common domain.

hypotheses: for each sign sigma, t^h_sigma = B(z_+, z_-)^T solves (t^h_sigma)' = A_Phi t^h_sigma - d t^h_sigma with z_+(0) = P(0), z_-(0) = 0 (homogeneous m = 1 problem, real amplitude), with pressure given by (7.13) at f_m = 0
geometric coordinates K_a, N_a, s_a as in (7.7); write t^h_sigma = x(e_r - s_a K_a) + y N_a
frame and error estimates of Lemma 7.1 on 0 < q < q_*; S_* sufficiently large

Every fixed derivative of this homogeneous solution in the coefficient variables or pulse coordinate is bounded by C_I S_*^{b_I} P(v). Its homogeneous pressure (7.13) with f = 0 has the extra factor eps^{1/2}.

c_lambda > 0 uniform lower bound for lambda
energy identity (1/2) d/dv |t|^2 = -g.(t_r(t_theta,t_z)) - eps k^2 |n_Phi|^2 |t|^2 (7.22)
eps k^2 ~ 1; carrier wavelength sqrt(Q)/k ~ Q^{1/2+h/2}; physical amplitude Q^{-A} sqrt(eps) = Q^{-1/2-h/2}
cites: Riccati equation for the frame ratio
entries.role: Constructs the two real homogeneous pulses (one per sign) that grow and then decay with the envelope P, with radial component comparable to P and controlled tangential direction; these are the building blocks of the leading covariance in Proposition 7.5.

hypotheses: for each slow box beta = (l, a), the homogeneous pulses of Lemma 7.4 form b_sigma = chi_g(xi_g) psi(v) t^h_sigma cos(k Phi_sigma), sigma = +/-, extended by zero off that sign's auxiliary rectangle; the two signs have disjoint auxiliary supports and share the slow cutoff eta_beta

a further single decrease of q_*

Define y = H^{-1} T_{0,*}, a_sigma = sqrt(y_sigma) (componentwise), W_0 = sqrt(eps) sum_sigma a_sigma b_sigma (7.24). For every fixed slow multi-index I on X_a < X < X_b: y_sigma >= c sqrt(S_*) zeta and |D^I y_sigma| <= C_I S_*^{b_I} zeta delta^{-a_I} (7.25). The a_sigma extend smoothly by zero at the shell edges. On the label's slow neighborhood the harmonic coefficients of W_0 obey the derivative and envelope estimates of W_{1/2}, and eta_beta W_0 in W_{1/2}. Before multiplication by the slow cutoff, C(W_0) = eps T_{0,*} (7.26). The decomposition uses only the order-zero target.

column formula H_sigma = (|det(v_r,v_t)|/2)(int chi_g^2 d xi_g) c_i int_0^{L_s} psi^2 x t^h_{sigma,tan} dv (7.27)
h_sigma = same with x^2, h_sigma ~ c_i sqrt(L_s) ~ S_*^{-1/2}
c sqrt(L_s) <= int psi^2 x^2 dv <= C sqrt(L_s); int psi^2 x^2 |v - L_s/2|/L_s dv <= C
H_sigma = h_sigma(-A_c N - sigma u_* K + e_sigma), |e_sigma| <= C S_*^{-1/2} (7.28)
reference cone T_N < 0, |T_K| < (u_*/A_c)(-T_N)
margin |T_K|/u_* <= (1 - eta_c)(-T_N/A_c) for fixed eta_c > 0
|det H| >= c/S_*, ||H^{-1}|| <= C sqrt(S_*), c sqrt(S_*)|T| <= y_sigma <= C sqrt(S_*)|T| (7.29)
physical assembly sum_beta Q^{-2A} eta_beta^2 eps T_{0,*} = q^{-A-1/2} T_0 (7.30), using sum_beta eta_beta^2 = 1

the fixed positive coefficients a_sigma and matrix H of Proposition 7.5, with bounds (7.25), (7.29)

With slow cutoffs shown explicitly: eta_beta L Sigma in W_{alpha-1/2}, B(W_0, L Sigma) = Sigma, and C(eta_beta L Sigma) in M_{2alpha-1} (7.32). The denominator a_sigma remains the fixed coefficient at every correction stage. No sign or size restriction on Sigma.

|D^I delta a_sigma| <= C_I eps^{alpha-1} S_*^{b'_I} sqrt(zeta) delta^{-a'_I} (7.33)

hypotheses: alpha in R, nonzero integer m; harmonic coefficient t_m in W_alpha independent of theta with n_Phi . t_m = 0

one D_r lowers the eps exponent by at most kappa_s, by (6.32)

identity div_* curl_* A = 0 via (D_r + R^{-1})(R^{-1} f) = R^{-1} D_r f

hypotheses: alpha, rho in R; normalized representatives W^as_0, L^as of (7.35)

normalized chart operators (6.6), Delta_0 = D_r^2 + R^{-1} D_r + D_z^2

vector Laplacian mean: Delta_0 - R^{-2} for r, theta components, Delta_0 for z

hypotheses: fixed correction stage j, exponent alpha, a band, its common torus y = Y_{i_0}, and e in {0,1,2}

hard_pages.why: Frame and cone condition: the displays for lambda_0^2 = -2F_0 N_theta(2F_0 N_theta + |g_0|), c_0 = lambda_0/(2F_0 N_theta), the cone inequality (7.1) |c_0 (T_{0,*}.K)/(T_{0,*}.N)| < 1 with T_{0,*}.N < 0, and the wave-number choice (p~/R_0, p_z) = B_s(K - sigma u_* g_0/(L_s|g_0|^2)) are all badly garbled in the extraction; I reconstructed them from the surrounding prose (c_0^2 = (v_s-2)/2, quotient |J_c|/(P_c - v_s)) and the consistency of (7.28)-(7.29) with Lemma C.1's cone test 2(P_c - v)^2 = (v-2)J_c^2.

Lemma 7.1 Step 3: the reference undamped 2x2 matrix [[0, 2F_0N_theta/(1+s^2)],[-(2F_0N_theta+|g_0|),0]] and the claim that its eigenvalues are +/-lambda with lambda = lambda_0/sqrt(1+s^2) had to be checked by hand (product of off-diagonal entries gives lambda_0^2/(1+s^2)); the argument for why the single threshold q_* works for all derivative orders (smallness S_*^2(eps+eps^2+k^{-1}) <= 1, 1 <= eps k^2 <= 4, det M = -2c_0 sqrt(1+s^2)) is dense.

Proposition 7.2 Steps 1-2: the net growth rate a_net(y) = lambda_0/sqrt(1+y^2) - lambda_0(1+y^2)/(1+u_*^2)^{3/2} and its v-derivative bound (between -C/L_s and -c/L_s using u_*/2 <= |s| <= 3u_*/2) giving the Gaussian envelope (7.16); the exact harmonic factor (7.18) and propagator bound (7.19) uniform in m; the polynomial-degree bookkeeping 1 + max{b_I, c_J + b'_{I-J}} in (7.20); and the common-torus path H_w with D_H v = O(S_*).

Proposition 7.5 Step 2: the solved squared amplitudes are printed as 'h_+y_+ = 2(-T_N/A_c 1 - T_K/u_*)' where the displaced '1' must be read as a factor 1/2 (I verified from H_sigma = h_sigma(-A_c N - sigma u_* K) that the correct factor is 1/2); also the relation between u_*, A_c = -c_0 sqrt(1+u_*^2), the margin eta_c, and the cone condition (7.1).
